ordered_diagnoses: Metastatic lung cancer to the heart

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive dyspnea on exertion with prior cardiac and oncologic history
salient_findings: ST elevation in leads V1, V2, and V3 on ECG
Large pericardial effusion with signs of impending cardiac tamponade on echocardiogram
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
Progressive dyspnea on exertion
History of multiple prior cardiac events
History of lung cancer with metastatic disease to the brain and myocardium
Received 2 drug-eluting stents to the right coronary artery 10 months prior
Denies chest pain at presentation
High-sensitivity cardiac troponin-T level was 40 ng/L
ECG shows normal sinus rhythm at 90 beats per minute
ECG shows ST elevation in leads V1, V2, and V3
Transthoracic echocardiogram shows well-circumscribed mass in the left ventricular mid-apical anteroseptum
Preserved left ventricular systolic function on echocardiogram
Large pericardial effusion with signs of impending cardiac tamponade on echocardiogram
Coronary angiography shows nonobstructive epicardial coronary artery disease

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of lung cancer with metastatic disease to the brain and myocardium, and the echocardiogram shows a large pericardial effusion with signs of impending cardiac tamponade, which is consistent with malignant pericardial effusion.

rejected.label: Cardiac tamponade
rejected.why: While the patient has signs of impending cardiac tamponade, the primary cause is more likely the malignant pericardial effusion due to metastatic disease.

rejected.label: Metastatic lung cancer to the heart
rejected.why: This is a broader diagnosis that encompasses the malignant pericardial effusion, but it does not specifically address the pericardial effusion and its implications.

rejected.label: Myopericarditis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and history do not strongly suggest an inflammatory process like myopericarditis, and the echocardiogram findings point more towards a malignant cause.

rejected.label: Constrictive pericarditis
rejected.why: There is no indication of chronic inflammation or scarring of the pericardium that would lead to constrictive pericarditis, and the acute presentation with a large pericardial effusion is more suggestive of a malignant process.
